properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (third pass): user-flagged overlap between HDY3/HDY1-2 and between E2/H1 and E3/H2 -- both were transcription errors (HDY1/2's diagonal notch was oversimplified into a plain rectangle that re-overlapped HDY3; E2/E3's bottom edge was misread as the row further south, landing on top of H1/H2). Re-read against the diagram's own gridlines and confirmed zero geometric overlap with the adjacent block this time. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (fourth pass): a user-flagged visual check found this block's west edge still sitting on real pavement/curbside parking even after the transform and buffer fixes above. Root-caused: this part of the site (A/B/D/E1-E4 cluster, farthest from this transform's anchor points near Illinois/Michigan St) has a real residual scale/shear error -- confirmed by comparing the pixel gap between Blocks A and B (50px) against the real-world distance the transform produces for it (~17.6m, implying a ~2.84 px/m local scale) versus the transform's own Illinois-Michigan calibration (~3.4 px/m) -- a ~20% local discrepancy. Rather than keep tuning the transform, the west edge was instead measured directly against georeferenced ESRI World Imagery (the same satellite basemap used elsewhere in this project for visual validation): the real paved curb/parking-lot edge was located by eye against a fine lon/lat grid overlaid on the orthophoto, and this edge's coordinate was moved to match it, leaving the rest of the diagram-derived shape unchanged. This is a targeted, ground-truthed fix for this one edge, not a re-validated transform -- other edges of this block still come from the diagram transform and carry that same residual uncertainty. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a batch color-region check found this block's committed shape was shifted east and extended too far south versus the diagram's actual fill. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [106,136,169], '70ft Max'), located the real gap at Maryland St separating this block from E3, and extracted a clean rectangular contour (OpenCV) at pixel (1463,1039)-(1702,1232). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Confirmed zero overlap with E3 (the two now sit cleanly on either side of the real Maryland St gap) or H1/H2; still overlaps Elevation Sky Park by ~850 m2 (an already-documented, expected overlap given ESP's own low-confidence placement).
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell well short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery -- 13m short at the SW corner, 25m short at the SE corner (a growing gap toward the east, consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors). Extended each south vertex independently by its own measured gap (rather than a uniform shift) so the block's south edge now reaches the real sidewalk across its full width, matching Figure 6.4.2's own convention of drawing blocks flush to the street.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Shown at 70 ft max per Figure 6.4.2, the same height tier as Parcel E3. NOTE: this differs from the separately-named 'Parcel E2' elsewhere in Pier 70 sourcing (a Kennerly Architecture and Planning-designed, ~280-unit residential building at 70 ft near Slipways Commons) -- that parcel sits in a different part of the site (per D4D Fig. 6.4.2's parcel labeling, the two 'E2' references may refer to distinct parcels, or reflect a labeling inconsistency between D4D figures; flagged as unresolved rather than merged). No construction-start source found for this block.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
